s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of unilateral weakness, speech disturbance, and visual disturbance with a history of cardiac arrhythmia and pacemaker implantation
salient_findings: Gaze deviation in the right eye
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 70s
Presented to the emergency department
Has a history of permanent atrial fibrillation
Has a history of complete heart block
Has a pacemaker implanted in the late 1990s
Pacemaker was upgraded to a biventricular system
Blood pressure was 147/75 mm Hg
Heart rate was 84 beats per minute
Respiratory rate was 16 breaths per minute
Oxygen saturation was 99% on room air
Computed tomography angiography showed a large middle cerebral artery territory
Electrocardiogram showed a ventricular-paced rhythm with ventricular bigeminy

shortlist.label: Ischemic stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with unilateral weakness, speech disturbance, and visual disturbance, consistent with ischemic stroke symptoms

shortlist.label: Cardioembolic stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of atrial fibrillation, which is a known risk factor for cardioembolic stroke

shortlist.label: Atrial fibrillation-related stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's history of atrial fibrillation and presentation with stroke symptoms make this a plausible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Middle cerebral artery occlusion
shortlist.why_kept: Computed tomography angiography showed a large middle cerebral artery territory, consistent with occlusion

shortlist.label: Thrombotic stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's presentation with unilateral weakness and speech disturbance could be consistent with thrombotic stroke

shortlist.label: Lacunar stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms could be consistent with lacunar stroke, although less likely given the large middle cerebral artery territory

shortlist.label: Cardiac embolism
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's history of atrial fibrillation and pacemaker implantation increase the risk of cardiac embolism

shortlist.label: Pacemaker-related thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's pacemaker implantation and history of atrial fibrillation increase the risk of pacemaker-related thrombosis

raw.rationale: The patient's history of permanent atrial fibrillation and the presence of a large middle cerebral artery territory on computed tomography angiography are consistent with a cardioembolic stroke, which occurs when a blood clot forms in the heart and travels to the brain, causing a stroke.

rejected.label: Ischemic stroke
rejected.why: Too broad, as cardioembolic stroke is a subtype of ischemic stroke

rejected.label: Atrial fibrillation-related stroke
rejected.why: Essentially the same as cardioembolic stroke in this context, but less specific

rejected.label: Middle cerebral artery occlusion
rejected.why: Describes the location of the stroke, but not the underlying cause

rejected.label: Thrombotic stroke
rejected.why: Refers to a blood clot forming in the blood vessels, which is not the primary mechanism in this case

rejected.label: Lacunar stroke
rejected.why: Typically involves smaller blood vessels and does not match the large territory involved

rejected.label: Cardiac embolism
rejected.why: While related, this term is more general and does not specifically imply a stroke

rejected.label: Pacemaker-related thrombosis
rejected.why: There is no indication that the pacemaker is directly related to the thrombosis or stroke
